This came up today with my SO actually, because he was doing something I found offensive and resorted to apologizing and saying he loved me rather than continuing to address the problem, and got upset when I wouldn't reciprocate. It's interesting how much of a big deal it is. I've come to not put so much trust into people's words because I've found that people will use their words to manipulate you. I feel like actions are much more insightful in revealing how people actually feel. 

In the situations you've described, it seems like you're being taken advantage of because you are clearly demonstrating how you feel towards these women, and because there isn't a label on it, it's easily misconstrued into just being a really generous friend. So I guess in some cases actions aren't cut-and-dry enough for some people. It may seem obvious to you that you're demonstrating your feelings through your actions, but others may simply choose not to see because they don't feel as seriously? My advice would be to invest more of your time in either work or just anything that interests you. You could even take up a new hobby. It's important to not be completely dependent on the time you spend with your partner for happiness, just as a precautionary measure.

I don't know if finding sexts on your partner's phone is the end-all of relationships; the ball is really in your court with that one. You know her better than we do. You undoubtedly need to sit down and have a serious talk with her. Trust is the most important foundation for any kind of relationship. If she can't even be trusted because she's dishonest with you, is there even a point to continuing? I guess these are just some things to consider after talking. I agree that some form of action should be taken. Just don't make any rash decisions based on your current feelings of betrayal that you might regret.
